target.title: Preserve Claude snapshots across CLI parse failures
target.body:
## Summary
- Preserve the existing Claude snapshot when repeated terminal CLI usage parse failures reach the failure gate, so the card can surface the failure without falling back to `Not fetched yet`.
- Gate parse-failure preservation on the terminal fetch attempt kind, so Web/OAuth parse failures still clear stale prior data once the failure gate surfaces the error.
- Keep a prior Max/Pro/Team/Ultra subscription snapshot visible when a later CLI probe returns a subscription-only response without quota data; Education/no-prior paths still use `Limits not available`.
- Add regression coverage for repeated CLI parse failures, subscription-only responses with prior subscription limits, and Web parse failures clearing stale snapshots.

Refs #2241.

## Tests
- `make check`
- `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD`
- `swiftc -parse Sources/CodexBar/UsageStore+Refresh.swift`
- `swiftc -parse Tests/CodexBarTests/ClaudeResilienceTests.swift`
- `swiftc -parse Tests/CodexBarTests/ClaudeEducationAvailabilityTests.swift`
- `swiftc -parse Tests/CodexBarTests/ClaudeWebRefreshResilienceTests.swift`

Attempted but not completed locally:
- `swift test --filter ClaudeResilienceTests`
- `swift test --filter ClaudeEducationAvailabilityTests`
- `swift test --skip-update --filter ClaudeResilienceTests`
- `swift test --skip-update --filter ClaudeWebRefreshResilienceTests`

Those SwiftPM runs stalled while resolving/downloading the Sparkle 2.9.3 binary artifact before tests executed. A direct `curl -L --max-time 60` download of the same artifact completed successfully earlier, so this looks like a local SwiftPM artifact resolver stall rather than a source-level test failure.

I did not run live Claude provider probes because the repository guidance says live provider probes, browser-cookie imports, and real account paths should not be run unless explicitly requested. The behavior here is covered with stubbed provider strategies and the hosted CI test shards.

## Compatibility Risk
Low. The change only affects Claude refresh failure publication when a prior Claude snapshot already exists, and the follow-up gate keeps stale Web/OAuth parse failures from being preserved as CLI data.

target.title: Show DeepSeek Platform usage with cost summary
target.body:
## Summary

- move DeepSeek Platform cost and token history from **Show credits & extra usage** to **Cost summary**
- show DeepSeek details inline for Inline, Submenu, and Both because DeepSeek has no cost submenu
- keep balance and browser sign-in guidance independent, while limiting detailed usage to the active token account

## Why

DeepSeek detailed Platform data is cost and token usage, but its fetch and rendering were gated by the unrelated credits/extras setting. Users could therefore authenticate successfully and see their balance while the available usage chart remained hidden.

This is a follow-up to #2135.

## Consent boundary

DeepSeek detailed usage continues to use the existing selected Chrome session. Enabling any non-Off **Cost summary** option is intentionally treated as consent to run that Platform usage probe and show its cost and token data inline. **Show credits & extra usage** no longer controls this probe. Turning Cost summary off disables detailed usage, while balance and sign-in guidance remain independent.

## Validation

- `swift test --filter MenuCardDeepSeekTests` (8 tests)
- `swift test --filter ProviderSettingsDescriptorTests` (36 tests)
- `make check`
- packaged DeepSeek CLI live probe with the signed-in Chrome profile
- manually checked a fresh build with DeepSeek Cost summary enabled and disabled

The full sharded test runner previously reached 46 green groups before its final mixed process/spend group hit the watchdog; the affected spend-controller suite passed separately (24 tests).

target.title: Document universal quota planning design
target.body:
## Summary

- define a universal, descriptor-driven quota-planning capability
- lead with learned full-session capacity (`N`), with theoretical capacity before reset (`M`) and an asymmetric reachability verdict
- isolate calibration by provider, account, pair, and fetch strategy while composing with pace per long metric
- specify the Codex, Claude, and Antigravity rollout, fail-closed behavior, lifecycle, presentation, and test boundaries

## Product decision

`N` is the headline because it answers how many full short-window allowance equivalents the remaining weekly quota can fund at the recently observed workload mix. `M` is the every-window-flat-out upper bound before reset and deliberately ignores workday settings; the existing pace engine remains the personalized projection.

`likelyStranded` is a conservative capacity conclusion, while `theoreticallyReachable` only says enough short-window capacity can become available under full use. A range-based verdict appears after at least two qualifying candidates; a lone candidate must include at least three percentage points of long-window movement before it can be displayed.

## Scope

This is a spec-only draft for design review. It does not change runtime behavior and does not close the feature issue.

Refs #2261 and the maintainer direction in https://github.com/steipete/CodexBar/issues/2261#issuecomment-5006555635

## Validation

- fresh product-reader review: pass
- fresh repository-architecture review: pass
- post-review lifecycle reader: pass
- post-review math/presentation reader: pass
- staged diff and whitespace checks: pass
- Swift tests not run (documentation-only change)
